content.text: All text entry in the properties panel seems to capture input. For example, after exiting focus on a text field, when I hit the space bar to start play, the text field is then re-focused, and the space is entered there. Instead, text fields in the app should be focus-averse. Only clicking or double-clicking a field should give it focus, and when the user hits enter or tab, that field should lose focus, and the broader app should then get focus, so pressing space or other keys operates the preview and play tools.

long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`

  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked

  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and

  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,

  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),

  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,

  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is

  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and

  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written

  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's

  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,

  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil

  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and

  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`

  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can

  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on

  claims it** (kpgalligan/framejob#35, 2026-09-24). The editor window routes
  a bare Space key-down (⇧ and ⇪ allowed, any other modifier untouched)
  before dispatch: it toggles play/pause unless the first responder is an
  editable `NSTextView` — every field editor, the Text tab's area, the
  canvas's inline editor, the Media tab's search field, so a Space is typed
  there — an `NSButton` or `NSSegmentedControl` (they press on Space by
  AppKit's own convention, reachable only under Full Keyboard Access, and an
  accessibility user keeps it), the canvas overlay (its own Space arms a pan
  and toggles on key-up, `PreviewCanvasView.handleKeyUp`), or a sheet is
  attached. An auto-repeat of a Space the window took is swallowed. A
  non-editable field editor (a selectable label), a slider, the window
  itself and every custom inspector control are the transport's. No MCP
  mirror: playback is view state, app/CLAUDE.md's exemption, and no play
  tool exists today; `set_playhead` stays the capability.
- **K-2 — In the canvas text editor Return applies, a modified Return is a
  new line, and Esc asks before dropping a change** (kpgalligan/framejob#37,
  2026-09-24). A bare Return or keypad Enter (⇪ allowed) commits the string
  and leaves the editor — the `set_text` it always sent, one undo step,
  nothing for an unchanged string; Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ inserts "\n",
  one rule, so ⌃Return no longer inserts AppKit's U+2028 line separator;
  while an input method holds marked text none of the three keys is routed.
  Esc leaves an unchanged edit at once; with the string changed a sheet
  asks: Cancel (Esc — back to typing, text kept), Revert (editor closed,
  clip untouched, no undo step), Apply (Return, the default — editor
  closed, the change applied, one undo step). Apply is the default because
  Return applies everywhere in the session and Apply is undoable; Revert is
  the one destructive answer and is never the default. The Text tab's
  `InspectorTextArea` keeps its form-field bargain (Return a newline,
  ⌘Return a commit in place, blur commits): it sits among fields that
  commit on blur, and a session that must be left is the canvas's alone. No
  MCP mirror: the keys are view state, `set_text` is the apply.

  attributes at view scale; an UPPERCASE text is edited as typed**
  (kpgalligan/framejob#117, 2026-09-30). The font, `.kern` and paragraph
  style are `LayerRenderers.textAttributes` at `video.scale × canvasScale`,

  chrome backdrop) and draws no stroke: a stroke moves no glyph, and a
  clip's colours can vanish on the backdrop. `case: upper` is shown as

"""kpgalligan/framejob#35 — Space toggles play wherever nothing is typing.

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
WORK = os.path.join(HERE, "work", "space-key")
PROBE_SWIFT = os.path.join(HERE, "space_key_probe.swift")
# The item composes through the app's Metal compositor, which loads
# `default.metallib` from the directory a bare swiftc binary is in
# (`mixed_audio_probe.py`'s `build_shader`).
SHADER = os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Resources", "Shaders", "Compositor.metal")
MOVIE = os.path.join(HERE, "media", "A.mov")
TICKS = e2.TICKS

BASELINE_EXPECTED = ["S2a", "S2b"]

RESULTS = []


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    RESULTS.append((name, bool(ok)))
    print(f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}")
    if detail:
        print("       " + detail)


def packages():
    """The card of the spec, 0–6 s, and after it 6 s of `media/A.mov`
    (README "Make the test media once"). The movie is there for ONE reason:
    a shape-only plan has no media track, so `Playback.startRebuild` drops
    the item and the transport refuses — measured, `playerLayer.player`
    had no `currentItem` over the card alone. The playhead starts at 0, on
    the card."""
    os.makedirs(WORK, exist_ok=True)
    e2.CHROME = WORK
    movie = {"id": 20, "path": MOVIE, "kind": "video", "duration": 10 * TICKS,
             "width": 640, "height": 360, "fps": [30, 1], "has_video": True,
             "has_audio": False}
    tail = {
        "id": 3, "track": 1, "start": 6 * TICKS, "duration": 6 * TICKS,
        "source": {"kind": "media", "media": 20, "in": 0, "reversed": False},
        "enabled": {"video": True, "audio": True}, "speed": 1.0,
        "video": e2.video_props(), "audio": None, "text": None, "shape": None,
        "actions": [], "transition_in": None, "name": None, "label": None,
    }
    card = e2.project([e2.clip(2, 0, e2.GREY, name="Card", duration=6 * TICKS), tail],
                      media=[movie])
    return {"card": e2.write_package("space-card", card)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The probe.


def build_shader(out, tree=ROOT):
    """The app's own `Compositor.metal` beside the binary, its entry points
    named as `tree`'s sources ask for them (`reference_build.tree_shader`)."""
    lib = os.path.join(out, "default.metallib")
    air = os.path.join(out, "Compositor.air")
    source = os.path.join(out, "Compositor.metal")
    with open(SHADER) as f:
        text = reference_build.tree_shader(tree, f.read())
    if not os.path.exists(source) or open(source).read() != text:
        with open(source, "w") as f:
            f.write(text)
    if os.path.exists(lib) and os.path.getmtime(source) < os.path.getmtime(lib):
        return lib, None
    step = subprocess.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metal", "-c", source, "-o", air],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if step.returncode != 0:
        return None, "xcrun metal failed: " + step.stderr.strip()[:300]
    step = subprocess.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metallib", air, "-o", lib],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if step.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(lib):
        return None, "xcrun metallib failed: " + step.stderr.strip()[:300]
    return lib, None


def build_probe(sources, out, reference=False):
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    entry = os.path.join(out, "main.swift")
    with open(PROBE_SWIFT) as f:
        source = f.read()
    if not os.path.exists(entry) or open(entry).read() != source:
        with open(entry, "w") as f:
            f.write(source)
    binary = os.path.join(out, "space-key-probe")
    shader, why = build_shader(out, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)))
    if shader is None:
        return None, why
    swift = sorted(os.path.join(sources, n) for n in os.listdir(sources)
                   if n.endswith(".swift") and n != "main.swift")
    lib = os.path.join(ROOT, "core", "target", "release", "libframejob_core.a")
    if not os.path.exists(lib):
        return None, f"{lib} is missing — run `cd core && cargo build --release` first"
    defines = reference_build.tree_defines(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)),
                                           ["HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD"] if reference else [])
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift + [entry], output=binary, defines=defines)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        errors = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        return None, "swiftc failed:\n       " + "\n       ".join(
            errors[:6] or ["(no error lines)"])
    if not built.reused:
        print(f"  probe built in {built.seconds:.0f} s")
    return binary, None


def probe_checks(sources, out, paths, reference=False):
    print("\n1 — the probe: S1 the route, S2 the app's own window")
    check("media/A.mov exists (README \"Make the test media once\")", os.path.exists(MOVIE),
          MOVIE)
    binary, error = build_probe(sources, out, reference)
    check("the probe builds over app/Sources", binary is not None, error or "")
    if binary is None:
        return None
    request = os.path.join(out, "request.json")
    answer = os.path.join(out, "answer.json")
    if os.path.exists(answer):
        os.remove(answer)
    with open(request, "w") as f:
        json.dump(paths, f, indent=2)
    secrets = os.path.join(out, "secrets")
    shutil.rmtree(secrets, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(secrets)
    with open(os.path.join(secrets, "anthropic-key"), "w") as f:
        f.write("space-key-dummy-key\n")
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", None)
    env.pop("RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY", None)
    result = subprocess.run([binary, request, answer, "-RCSecretFolder", secrets,
                             "-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed", "NO"],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300, env=env)
    if result.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(answer):
        check("the probe runs", False, (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip()[-400:])
        return None
    with open(answer) as f:
        rows = json.load(f)["rows"]
    groups = ["S2a", "S2b", "S2c", "S2d", "S2e", "S2f"]
    if not reference:
        groups = ["S1", "S2g"] + groups + ["S2h"]
    check(f"the probe answers every row group ({', '.join(groups)} present)",
          all(any(r["name"].startswith(g + " ") for r in rows) for g in groups),
          f"{len(rows)} rows")
    for row in rows:
        check(row["name"], row["ok"], row["detail"])
    return rows


def baseline(commit):
    began = time.time()
    tree = os.path.join(WORK, "baseline")
    if os.path.exists(tree):
        shutil.rmtree(tree)
    os.makedirs(tree)
    archive = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "archive", commit, "app/Sources",
                              "app/Bridging"],
                             capture_output=True)
    if archive.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: git archive {commit} failed: "
              f"{archive.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    untar = subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", tree], input=archive.stdout,
                           capture_output=True)
    if untar.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: tar failed: {untar.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    print(f"BASELINE {commit}: app/Sources in {os.path.relpath(tree, ROOT)}, built with "
          "-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD")
    rows = probe_checks(os.path.join(tree, "app", "Sources"),
                        os.path.join(tree, "out"), packages(), reference=True)
    elapsed = time.time() - began
    if rows is None:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: the probe did not build or run over {commit}, "
              f"{elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 1
    failed = sorted({r["name"].split(" ")[0] for r in rows if not r["ok"]})
    absent = [r["name"] for r in rows
              if r["name"].startswith(("S1 ", "S2g ", "S2h "))]
    structural = [n for n, ok in RESULTS if not ok and not n.startswith("S")]
    if failed == sorted(BASELINE_EXPECTED) and not absent and not structural:
        print(f"BASELINE PASS: exactly {', '.join(BASELINE_EXPECTED)} FAILED on {commit} and "
              f"nothing else did, {elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 0
    print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: failed {failed} (want {BASELINE_EXPECTED}), S1/S2g/S2h rows "
          f"present {absent}, other failures {structural}, {elapsed:.0f} s")
    return 1


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) == 3 and sys.argv[1] == "--baseline":
        return baseline(sys.argv[2])
    if len(sys.argv) != 1:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    print("#35 — Space toggles play wherever nothing is typing")
    probe_checks(os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Sources"), os.path.join(WORK, "probe"),
                 packages())
    good = sum(1 for _, ok in RESULTS if ok)
    print(f"\n{good}/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
    return 0 if RESULTS and good == len(RESULTS) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Spec §11 K-4 — typing in the editor window is focus-averse.

    python3 tools/proof/text_focus_proof.py
    python3 tools/proof/text_focus_proof.py --baseline d4537dc

One instrument, the probe `text_focus_probe.swift`, compiled AS `main.swift`
over every file in `app/Sources` but the app's own `main.swift` on
`swift_build.py`'s line (a probe that will not build is a scored FAILURE,
never an exit). F1 asks `TextFocus` row by row; F2 drives the app's own
editor window with synthesized keys and clicks and reads the first
responder, each field's commit and whether Space then plays; F3 is the
Assistant composer's Return in a window of its own.

The fixture and the shader are `space_key_proof.py`'s (the card, then 6 s of
`media/A.mov`, so the transport has an item to play), written under this
proof's own work folder.

`--baseline <commit>` builds the same probe over `git archive <commit>
app/Sources` with `-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD` (F1 compiled out) and exits 0
only when EXACTLY the rows in `BASELINE_EXPECTED` fail there and no F1 row is
present — the rows that measure K-4, failing on the tree before it; the
others (a click inside the field, an option field's margin, ⇧Return's new
line, a refused send) are guards that held before and must still hold.

The probe runs with a DUMMY key in a `-RCSecretFolder` of its own (so the
composer shows), `-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed NO`, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and
RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY popped from its environment: no person's key is read.
"""

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import reference_build  # noqa: E402
import space_key_proof as space  # noqa: E402  (the card fixture, the shader)
import swift_build  # noqa: E402

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
WORK = os.path.join(HERE, "work", "text-focus")
PROBE_SWIFT = os.path.join(HERE, "text_focus_probe.swift")

# F2a–F2c the toolbar timecode's Return, Tab and ⇧Tab; F2d–F2e the clip
# header's name on Return and on a click on the timeline; F2g an option
# field's Tab; F2i–F2j the Text tab's area's Return and Tab; F2k the
# composer's Tab; F3a the composer after a send.
BASELINE_EXPECTED = ["F2a", "F2b", "F2c", "F2d", "F2e", "F2g", "F2i", "F2j", "F2k", "F3a"]

RESULTS = []


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    RESULTS.append((name, bool(ok)))
    print(f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}")
    if detail:
        print("       " + detail)


def packages():
    space.WORK = WORK
    return space.packages()


def build_probe(sources, out, reference=False):
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    entry = os.path.join(out, "main.swift")
    with open(PROBE_SWIFT) as f:
        source = f.read()
    if not os.path.exists(entry) or open(entry).read() != source:
        with open(entry, "w") as f:
            f.write(source)
    binary = os.path.join(out, "text-focus-probe")
    shader, why = space.build_shader(out, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)))
    if shader is None:
        return None, why
    swift = sorted(os.path.join(sources, n) for n in os.listdir(sources)
                   if n.endswith(".swift") and n != "main.swift")
    lib = os.path.join(ROOT, "core", "target", "release", "libframejob_core.a")
    if not os.path.exists(lib):
        return None, f"{lib} is missing — run `cd core && cargo build --release` first"
    defines = reference_build.tree_defines(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)),
                                           ["HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD"] if reference else [])
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift + [entry], output=binary, defines=defines)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        errors = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        return None, "swiftc failed:\n       " + "\n       ".join(
            errors[:6] or ["(no error lines)"])
    if not built.reused:
        print(f"  probe built in {built.seconds:.0f} s")
    return binary, None


def probe_checks(sources, out, paths, reference=False):
    print("\n1 — the probe: F1 the rule, F2 the app's own window, F3 the composer's Return")
    check("media/A.mov exists (README \"Make the test media once\")", os.path.exists(space.MOVIE),
          space.MOVIE)
    binary, error = build_probe(sources, out, reference)
    check("the probe builds over app/Sources", binary is not None, error or "")
    if binary is None:
        return None
    request = os.path.join(out, "request.json")
    answer = os.path.join(out, "answer.json")
    if os.path.exists(answer):
        os.remove(answer)
    with open(request, "w") as f:
        json.dump(paths, f, indent=2)
    secrets = os.path.join(out, "secrets")
    shutil.rmtree(secrets, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(secrets)
    with open(os.path.join(secrets, "anthropic-key"), "w") as f:
        f.write("text-focus-dummy-key\n")
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", None)
    env.pop("RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY", None)
    result = subprocess.run([binary, request, answer, "-RCSecretFolder", secrets,
                             "-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed", "NO"],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300, env=env)
    if result.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(answer):
        check("the probe runs", False, (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip()[-400:])
        return None
    with open(answer) as f:
        rows = json.load(f)["rows"]
    groups = ["F2a", "F2b", "F2c", "F2d", "F2e", "F2f", "F2g", "F2h", "F2i", "F2j", "F2k",
              "F3a", "F3b"]
    if not reference:
        groups = ["F1"] + groups
    check(f"the probe answers every row group ({', '.join(groups)} present)",
          all(any(r["name"].startswith(g + " ") for r in rows) for g in groups),
          f"{len(rows)} rows")
    for row in rows:
        check(row["name"], row["ok"], row["detail"])
    return rows


def baseline(commit):
    began = time.time()
    tree = os.path.join(WORK, "baseline")
    if os.path.exists(tree):
        shutil.rmtree(tree)
    os.makedirs(tree)
    archive = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "archive", commit, "app/Sources",
                              "app/Bridging"],
                             capture_output=True)
    if archive.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: git archive {commit} failed: "
              f"{archive.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    untar = subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", tree], input=archive.stdout,
                           capture_output=True)
    if untar.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: tar failed: {untar.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    print(f"BASELINE {commit}: app/Sources in {os.path.relpath(tree, ROOT)}, built with "
          "-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD")
    rows = probe_checks(os.path.join(tree, "app", "Sources"),
                        os.path.join(tree, "out"), packages(), reference=True)
    elapsed = time.time() - began
    if rows is None:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: the probe did not build or run over {commit}, "
              f"{elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 1
    failed = sorted({r["name"].split(" ")[0] for r in rows if not r["ok"]})
    absent = [r["name"] for r in rows if r["name"].startswith("F1 ")]
    structural = [n for n, ok in RESULTS if not ok and not n.startswith("F")]
    if failed == sorted(BASELINE_EXPECTED) and not absent and not structural:
        print(f"BASELINE PASS: exactly {', '.join(BASELINE_EXPECTED)} FAILED on {commit} and "
              f"nothing else did, {elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 0
    print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: failed {failed} (want {sorted(BASELINE_EXPECTED)}), F1 rows "
          f"present {absent}, other failures {structural}, {elapsed:.0f} s")
    return 1


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) == 3 and sys.argv[1] == "--baseline":
        return baseline(sys.argv[2])
    if len(sys.argv) != 1:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    print("K-4 — typing in the editor window is focus-averse")
    probe_checks(os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Sources"), os.path.join(WORK, "probe"),
                 packages())
    good = sum(1 for _, ok in RESULTS if ok)
    print(f"\n{good}/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
    return 0 if RESULTS and good == len(RESULTS) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

## Sending a message

Type in the field ("Ask about or edit this project…") and press Return or click **Send**. The field starts one line high and grows to five lines as you type. Past five lines it scrolls.

| Key | In the message field |
|---|---|
| Return or keypad Enter | Sends the message. While the assistant is working or waiting for an answer, it beeps instead. |
| ⇧Return, ⌘Return, ⌥Return, ⌃Return | Starts a new line |
| Tab, ⇧Tab | Moves focus to the next or previous control |
| ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z | Undoes or redoes your typing. Typing never lands on the project's undo stack. |

The field empties once the message is sent. If the conversation cannot start (for example, the key was removed), the reason appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the field.

While a turn runs, **Send** reads **Stop**. See [Stopping a turn](#stopping-a-turn).

content.text:
Text fields in the editor window now let go of the keys. After Return, Tab or a click anywhere outside the field, the value is applied and Space plays straight away. The gate and the proofs all pass; nothing is committed.

**What was wrong.** Two things, both hidden because these fields draw no focus ring:
- **Return:** the value was saved, then AppKit put the cursor straight back in the field with its text selected. That's the "re-focus" you saw: the next Space replaced the text.
- **Clicking the timeline:** the timeline never takes the keyboard, so the field quietly kept it, with nothing saved.

**The fix.** One rule in `app/Sources/EditorWindow.swift`, checked before each key or click reaches anything else. It covers every text field in the window (inspector fields, the toolbar timecode, the Media search, timeline renames, the canvas text editor, the Assistant message field), and new fields get it without extra code:
- A click outside the field you're typing in ends the typing. The title bar is excluded.
- Tab ends it in any field. Return ends it in one-line fields.
- Each field saves through its normal path, once, as it does when it loses focus.

**Behaviour changes to check:**
- **Text tab's Content area:** Return now applies the text and lets go, and ⇧Return starts a new line, matching the canvas text editor. ⌘Return is now a new line; it used to apply the text and stay in the field. This reverses part of an earlier recorded decision, so I wrote it up as a new one (K-4 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/chrome-inspector-keys.md`).
- **Assistant message field:** after Return sends, the keys go back to the editor, so Space plays while the assistant works. If Return only beeps because it's busy, the field keeps them.
- **Full Keyboard Access:** I kept Tab moving between controls when it's on. Otherwise a keyboard-only user could never get past the first text field. Return and click-away still let go. This is the same exception the Space rule already makes for buttons.
- Esc is unchanged. Sheets, Settings and the Welcome window are separate windows and keep the normal dialog keys.

**Verification:**
- **New proof:** `tools/proof/text_focus_proof.py` drives the app's real editor window with simulated keys and clicks and passes 57/57.
- **Bug reproduced:** run on the code before the fix, it fails exactly the 8 rows that show your bug. In one, Return saved the clip's name and the field took the keys straight back, so Space was typed into it.
- **Mutants:** I broke each decision in the change one at a time (8 in all), and the proof caught every one.
- **Other proofs:** `make gate` passes; the Space-key proof passes 29/29 and the Assistant tab proof 26/26 against the Release app.

**For you to try:** a simulated event isn't a real keyboard and mouse, so I added a check to `docs/manual-checks.md` (TL-16) covering the steps you described. I also updated the user guide pages and the proofs README.
